nodes.name: NiFeCr electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: Nickel foam (NF, 110 ppm, 1.0 mm thickness, exposed geometric area: 1.0 × 1.0 cm²) was used as working electrode. The electrodeposition was carried out at the applied potential of -1.0 V vs Ag/AgCl for 900 s, in an electrodeposition bath containing 12 mM nickel nitrate hexahydrate, 3 mM iron nitrate nonahydrate and 6 mM chromium nitrate nonahydrate. During the electrodeposition process, locally generated OH⁻ ions via the reduction of nitrate react with Ni²⁺, Fe³⁺ and Cr³⁺, and co-precipitate onto the substrate (i.e. NF), forming a light-brown-colored coating (denoted as NiFeCr/NF). Thereafter the electrodeposited electrode was thoroughly rinsed by water and air-dried.
nodes.source_text: The NiFeCr catalyst materials were obtained via electrodeposition in a standard three-electrode configuration... forming a light-brown-colored coating (denoted as NiFeCr/NF). Thereafter the electrodeposited electrode was thoroughly rinsed by water and air-dried.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe catalyst shows doublet Ni-O peaks shifting to ~475 and ~555 cm⁻¹ at ≥0.5 V indicating NiOOH formation; NiFeCr shows stronger peak at ~555 cm⁻¹ indicating more β-NiOOH phase; pristine NiFeCr has more hydroxide (peak ~680 cm⁻¹) and less oxide structures.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Operando Raman analysis (Fig. 3a) was then applied to reveal the active intermediates on NiFeCr and NiFe catalysts during water oxidation... It is found the peak intensity at ~555 cm⁻¹ is stronger than ~475 cm⁻¹ in NiFeCr catalyst, suggesting more amount of β-NiOOH phase is produced during OER.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe catalyst: Fe remains 3+ valence, Ni oxidizes to Ni³⁺⁻⁴⁺ with 4.0 eV edge shift, shorter Fe-O and Ni-O bonds in Fe-sub-β-NiOOH intermediate; NiFeCr catalyst: Fe 3+, Ni minimal shift (0.2 eV), Cr oxidizes to Cr⁶⁺ with shorter Cr-O bond at 1.2 Å in Cr,Fe-sub-β-NiOOH.
